Subject: Private VPC deployment — initial requirements and commercial questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We are keen to move forward with a private VPC deployment for our analytics cluster (approx. 4 nodes, 32GB token throughput use case). Procurement has a few immediate asks before we start legal redlines:

- Can you share the current MSA with any existing addenda for on-prem/VPC deployments?
- We need a clear summary of license scope (runtime, operator access limits, redistribution rights).
- Our security team will require an operator-proof or escrow-like assurance for a failover scenario — please outline options (witnessed snapshot, sealed escrow, steward access).
- Please confirm the proposed SLOs and any SLA carveouts for on-prem.

Attached is our procurement punchlist for vendor engagements; this will guide our legal review. Please include timelines for legal/legal-tech review and a procurement order form sample.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Cardinal Health Systems

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — initial requirements and commercial questions

Hi — really appreciate the clear list. Attaching our redline baseline and a draft order form to get the ball rolling. High level plan:

1) License scope: Redwood provides a runtime license to run verified model images in your VPC. We do not transfer model weights; license covers execution-only for the agreed tenant(s). We will propose a limited derivative carve (no redistribution).

2) Operator access / failover: two viable approaches — (A) witnessed snapshot and handoff (on-prem witness event, limited window), or (B) sealed snapshot + escrow steward with multi-party unlocking. Naomi is looping in legal options below.

3) Audit/evidence: we can provide an evidence binder (hashes, runbook, operator checklist) and a temporary console read-only audit window for a specified period. Exact items in the binder are in the attached OrderForm_draft and MSA_redlines_v1.

Next steps: Naomi and Jordan will lift legal redlines and propose language tonight. If the commercial points look OK, I can send a DocuSign link for the initial order form (S1) and schedule a technical runbook sync.

Deliverables attached: MSA_redlines_v1.pdf, OrderForm_draft.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed redlines for Cardinal Health VPC addendum

Team — quick summary for what I recommend we send to Cardinal after Karthik's commercial alignment:

- License scope: tighten to 'Execution-Only License' with explicit prohibition on model extraction or redistribution. Add a definition section for 'Operator' vs. 'Customer Administrator'.
- Audit & evidence: offer a "sealed-snapshot" pathway as default (witness optional). For highly regulated customers we can offer a witnessed snapshot at a defined cost and scheduling SLA.
- Escrow-lite: propose a 3rd-party steward (trusted cryptographic custodian) holding sealed snapshots and a two-party release process (customer + Redwood signoff) to avoid full source/weight transfer.
- Operator access: propose time-bound, role-based console access for audits; no persistent operator credentials in customer VPC other than ephemeral certs generated for the event.
- SLA carveouts: clearly enumerate maintenance windows and emergency remediation that may impact local runtime and exclude those from credit calculations.

I attached a redline with inline comments (MSA_redlines_legal_v2.pdf) and a short evidence checklist we can share to set expectations for the initial audit window.

If you want, include an explicit pricing line in the OrderForm for witnessed events and steward escrow fees so Procurement has a one-stop commercial cost.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
